content.text:
The baseline is green (9/9). Here is what I found in `ConfigLoader`, and the plan:

- `intValue` and `duration` replace bad values with defaults. That is exactly the bug that bit ops.
- `uri` returns `null` on a bad URL, and a missing `upstream.url` also becomes `null` through a swallowed NPE.
- `read` swallows a missing or unreadable file, so the relay runs on defaults.
- `Boolean.parseBoolean` maps any typo to `false`.
- Unknown keys are ignored, so a misspelled key name is also silent.

My approach: collect every problem, then throw one `ConfigException` that lists them all with the file name. `Main` prints that to stderr and exits with status 2 before any work starts. I'm also rejecting unknown keys, since a typo'd key name is the same class of failure. That one can break an existing file that has extra keys, so I'll call it out in the summary.

# relay

A small service that reads messages from standard input and forwards each one to an upstream endpoint, with a
bounded work queue, a worker pool and retries. In this checkout the upstream is simulated by printing the
request to standard output.

## Running

    cp config.example.properties config.properties
    java tools/RunTests.java                       # compiles into build/classes first
    java -cp build/classes com.acme.relay.Main config.properties < messages.txt

Without an argument the service reads `config.properties` from the working directory.

## Configuration

| Key                  | Required | Default | Meaning                                                     |
|----------------------|----------|---------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `upstream.url`       | yes      |         | URL the messages are forwarded to                           |
| `api.token`          | yes      |         | Token sent to the upstream                                  |
| `worker.threads`     | no       | `4`     | Number of delivery threads, at least 1                      |
| `queue.capacity`     | no       | `1000`  | Messages waiting for a free worker, at least 1              |
| `retry.max-attempts` | no       | `3`     | Retries after the first failed delivery, 0 or more          |
| `request.timeout`    | no       | `30s`   | Time limit per delivery: a whole number plus `ms`, `s`, `m` |
| `metrics.enabled`    | no       | `false` | `true` or `false`: print delivery counts on shutdown        |

## Tests

    java tools/RunTests.java

The runner compiles `src/main/java` and `src/test/java` and runs every JUnit 5 test. It needs
`lib/junit-platform-console-standalone.jar`.

content.text:
The relay now refuses to start on a bad config. It prints every problem with the file name and exits with status 2 before it reads any messages. The test suite passes (19 of 19, up from 9) and I checked the real `Main` entry point against bad, missing, and valid files.

For the typo from last week, `worker.threads=4a` now fails with:

```
Relay not started: invalid configuration in config.properties (2 problems):
  - worker.threads must be a whole number, got '4a'
  - metrics.enabled must be true or false, got 'ture'
```

What changed in `ConfigLoader`, which was the source of the silent fallbacks:
- **Bad values** (non-numbers, values below the minimum, bad timeout units, and misspelled booleans) are errors. They used to fall back to defaults or `false`.
